newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end up 3.31 pct, led by power, telcoms.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end up 3.31 pct, led by power, telcoms.

text.p: Brazilian stocks, led by power and telecommunications shares, closed sharply higher in heavy trading Monday, as investors showed renewed confidence in the economy, brokers said
"The market opened higher and rose steadily all day," a local trader said.

The Sao Paulo bolsa's Bovespa index of 47 most-traded shares pared some gains in the afternoon but rode a wave of late buying to end up 3.31 percent at 12,938 points. Turnover reached 1.165 billion reais ($1.08 billion).
With the day's sharp gains, the bolsa has all but retraced the ground lost in mid-July when share prices dived amid fears of a currency devaluation and a wave of profit-taking.
Brokers said Monday's session was marked by steady, strong trade with low volatility as a scarcity of major market-moving news kept investors tranquil.
"There was no news in Brazil and that allowed the market to operate calmly," a dealer said.
He said there was further speculation that the privatization of the federal telecom system, Telebras, would take place sooner than had been expected.
Telebras' preferred shares, which accounted for more than 60 percent of total volume, jumped 4.17 percent to end at 162.50 reais, while its common stock surged 4.95 percent to 162.50 reais.
Preferred shares of the telecom company's Sao Paulo unit, Telesp. soared 5.59 percent to end at 378 reais while its Rio de Janeiro operator, Telerj, leapt 7.89 percent to end at 164 reais.
Power sector shares also rose, with the bolsa's Electrical Energy Index climbing 1.68 percent to 3,560 points. It was led by 4.37 percent gain by Eletrobras' preferred, which closed at 645 reais .
Volume was boosted by strong activity in state oil company Petrobras, whose preferred shares surged 2.5 percent to end 328 reais.

They also said Brazilian stocks in general benefited from investment bank reports saying it was a mistake to liken Brazil's financial and economic health to that of Asian countries that announced devaluations.
Speculation that Brazil would follow suit with its own devaluation led to sharp declines in local markets earlier this month.
Brokers forecast trading Tuesday would mirror Monday's strong steadily rising trend on declining volatility and growing confidence.
